title: Dataplex: Breaking Schema Changes & New Data Product Insights
summary: Dataplex introduces breaking changes by making several documentation and entry-related properties read-only. Developers must update their code if they were writing to these fields. On the upside, new generated data product insights are now available, and batch metadata change requests gain a `deferredValidation` option.
details:
Several properties across Dataplex schemas have been made read-only, constituting breaking changes. Specifically, the `dataProductResult` property in `GoogleCloudDataplexV1DataDocumentationResult`, `assetDescriptions`, `overview`, and `queries` within `GoogleCloudDataplexV1DataDocumentationResultDataProductResult`, `overview` and `resource` in `GoogleCloudDataplexV1DataDocumentationResultDataProductResultAssetDescription`, and `entryGroupType` in `GoogleCloudDataplexV1Entry` are now immutable. If your applications previously wrote to these fields, they will now fail and require updates.

On the feature front, Dataplex now provides richer, automatically generated insights for data products. The `GoogleCloudDataplexV1DataDocumentationResult` schema includes a new `dataProductResult` field, which is an output-only `GoogleCloudDataplexV1DataDocumentationResultDataProductResult` object. This new object contains `assetDescriptions` (generated descriptions for assets), `overview` (a detailed description for the data product), and `queries` (sample SQL queries). These additions enhance the discoverability and understanding of your data products.

Furthermore, the `GoogleCloudDataplexV1RequestBatchMetadataChangeRequest` now supports an optional `deferredValidation` boolean parameter. Setting this to `true` allows for deferring reference validation until the change request is approved, providing more flexibility in batch metadata operations. The `lookupEntryLinks` method also saw scope adjustments, now explicitly supporting `dataplex.read-write` and `dataplex.readonly`.
